title: Rapid Fabrication of Custom Microfluidic Devices for Research and Educational Applications
protocol: Design an application for the devices and list required channel/chamber components.
Hand-draw each layer of the device, considering its functionality.
Draw final designs using computer software that allows line and shape drawing.
Use black, solid lines and shapes devoid of shades for clarity.
Import each layer into the craft cutter software via screen capture and drag-and-drop.
Create a new document in the craft cutter software (free download).
Drop the image file onto the mat displayed in the software.
Enlarge the image to facilitate processing by pulling from a corner.
Recognize the design using the trace function in the craft cutter software.
Select the Trace icon (shape of a butterfly) on the right side of the window.
Completely select the imported designs.
Choose the Trace Preview option labeled outline.
Adjust the Threshold and Scale settings to match the yellow trace with the design.
Select Trace from the Trace menu once the red contour matches the design.
Delete the imported image if the red contour accurately represents the design.
Size the device by selecting the traced design and using the grid provided in the software.
Pull to adjust the width and length of channels and chambers.
Draw small lines temporarily, using the design palette on the left side, to measure dimensions within the device.
Ensure functional channel-width dimensions range from 100 µm to 900 µm.
Adjust dimensions after testing initial prototypes if necessary.
Size all layers proportionally to ensure proper alignment during assembly.
Select the square tool on the shape drawing menu.
Draw a square/rectangle around each layer of the device.
Make sure the square/rectangle is of the same size for all layers.
Create a separate top layer containing access ports to the channels.
Select the drawing tool on the left side of the screen.
Draw circles over the inlet and outlet ports of the design.
Copy and paste both the original design and the circles.
Erase the channels from the underlying device.
Arrange all layers to be cut on the displayed mat.
Apply a single PET/EVA film onto the adhesive cutting mat.
Make sure the adhesive side faces up and the plastic side faces down.
Flatten the film against the mat, removing all air trapped.
Align the edge of the cutting mat to the line indicated on the cutter.
Load the mat by pressing Load Mat on the cutter.
Select a cutting setting between 3 and 5, depending on film thickness.
Connect the cutter USB cable to the computer.
Select the SEND tab and choose a cutting setting.
Click Send to begin cutting.
Ensure there is enough room in the back of the cutter for the mat to move unimpeded.
Unload the mat by selecting Unload on the cutter after cutting is finished.
Place the cutting mat next to a clean surface.
Use tweezers with gloved hands to lift each layer of the microfluidics device off the cut mat carefully around turns and bends.
Order the layers according to their top-to-bottom position in the device.
Cut small pieces (~3 mm x 10 mm) of double-sided tape for temporarily attaching the layers together.
Superimpose the bottom layer first.
Add a small piece of double-sided tape to a corner between layers, away from any channels or inlets/outlets.
Use a wire jig to facilitate alignment of layers in devices with more than 4 layers.
Ensure that the adhesive side of the film always faces the inside portion of the device.
Set the laminator to the desired thickness setting; use the 5-mil setting for devices with 4 or more layers.
Run the device through the laminating rollers, placing the end with double-sided tape first.
Use a rotary tool and a 1/32 in. drill bit to cut a small hole through the center of a furniture bumper.
Alternatively, use a 1 mm biopsy punch to perforate the bumpers.
Cut holes using revolving punch pliers for larger perforations when the bumper is used as a "reservoir" for liquids or other biologicals.
Remove any debris from the inlet/outlet ports with a pair of small tweezers.
Align bumpers with the inlet/outlet ports on the laminated device.
Position the adhesive face of the bumper facing the open inlet/outlet on the device.
Adhere the bumper behind the device to complete the assembly.
Access channel/chamber architectures through the perforated bumpers (ports).
Attach laboratory or medical/surgical tubing to a plastic connector or blunt needle for fluid introduction.
Use a standard pipette and tip or PEEK tubing without adaptors for fluid introduction.
Perform infusion or drawing of fluids using syringes and tubing with peristaltic pumps.
Set different flow rate settings according to the device and experiment.
